figures.caption: Fig. 2: End-to-end workflow used in our study: pretrain on pooled data, fine-tune per CFUT, then testing with UOF/WODF assessment

TABLE II: Hyperparameters of the encoder (edge-biased graph Transformer) and the FiLM head. Pretraining uses 23 IBM devices with ≥ 7 qubits (500 epochs backend-wise, 1000 epochs general). Fine-tuning on each CFUT updates only the FiLM head; the encoder is frozen (eval).

TABLE III: Backend view. Entries are Hellinger distances H averaged over all CFUTs for each backend (mean ± sd; lower is better). RIB←Q is the relative improvement of the backend-wise model over QOIN, the strongest baseline. RIG←Q is the relative improvement of the general model over QOIN. The last 3 columns report selected backend-level indicators used in the failure-mode analysis: readout-error heterogeneity (σro), average two-qubit gate error (µ2q), and two-qubit gate-error heterogeneity (σ2q).

Fig. 1: Model architecture overview. Left: Graph Transformer encoder with edge-biased attention. Right: FiLM head that conditions on observation features and an optional learned backend embedding (unified model). Here, MLP denotes a multi-layer perceptron, and FFN denotes the feed-forward network.
